refs.name: blank-page
refs.title: Blank Page — Motion Graphics Prompt Expander (Midjourney for Motion)
refs.tagline: Expands a rough one-line idea into an expressive motion-graphics brief with a visual look, style references, and a sequence of choreographed beats so the first draft is already compelling.
refs.stylePrompt: Expand a one-line motion-graphics prompt ('/blank-page' by @blak3shao / StewdioAI style): (1) Art Direction & Palette — define a bold primary stage color (e.g. deep cobalt #002699 or obsidian #0B0D12), tactile surface treatment (pixel/voxel, frosted glass, or editorial vector), and accent highlights; (2) Focal Hero Object — center a single expressive physical or UI object before introducing text; (3) Beat-by-Beat Choreography (0.0s–5.0s) — specify exact entrance physics, camera push/pull, state morph, and clean resolve beat so the first generated draft feels art-directed rather than a generic slide.

refs.name: pr-writing
refs.title: PR Writing — Evidence-First Pull Request Descriptions
refs.tagline: Write pull request descriptions ordered for a skimmer that prove the change works with real evidence (same-crop before/after UI + phone width, real CLI output, measured benchmarks) and end with a plain-English ELI5.
refs.stylePrompt: Write an evidence-first Pull Request description ('pr-writing' by @hugorcd style): (1) The problem in one plain paragraph with real numbers when available; (2) What changed, grouped by area rather than a commit list; (3) Evidence table matching the change type — for UI: side-by-side Before vs After screenshots at identical viewport & crop plus a mobile/phone-width pair and short video for hover/motion; for CLI/build: verbatim command output + exit code; for perf/AI: measured latency/cost rubric on both sides; (4) Reviewer details, trade-offs, and honest limitations; (5) ELI5 summary in 2-3 plain sentences.

refs.name: stack-diagram
refs.title: Stack Diagram — Architecture Diagrams with Official Logos
refs.tagline: Describe your tech stack in a single sentence and get a light + dark architecture diagram with official vendor logos, rendered as a standalone HTML file, PNGs, and React component.
refs.stylePrompt: Render a dual light/dark architecture stack diagram ('stack-diagram' by caru-ini style): (1) subtle blueprint grid background (#F8FAFC in light mode, #0D1117 in dark mode); (2) crisp white rounded-square icon tiles (64×64, rx=14, 1px subtle border and soft shadow) so official brand/vendor SVG logos preserve their authentic colors in both themes; (3) bold node title + monospace role subtitle underneath each tile; (4) translucent rounded boundary containers for workspaces/clouds (e.g. 'pnpm workspace', 'GitHub') with brand icon + label in top-left; (5) orthogonal/straight connector arrows with inline monospace edge verbs ('git push', 'publish', 'turbo run', 'pre-commit').

refs.name: coworkers
refs.title: Coworkers — Inline Skill Installer & Cloudflare AI Teammates
refs.tagline: AI teammates on Cloudflare Durable Objects that each get their own computer, browser, and conversational 'Install skills?' approval card (npx skills add https://github.com/emilkowalski/skills) with per-bot or all-bots scoping.
refs.stylePrompt: Design an inline 'Install skills?' conversational approval card inside an AI agent chat ('Coworkers' by @fayazara style): (1) warm light-gray rounded container (#F6F6F5) nested inside a clean white chat canvas; (2) header with bold title 'Install skills?' and muted repo + pinned SHA subtitle (e.g. 'emilkowalski/skills · a81dbca'); (3) skill count + 'Select all' action above a white rounded list card containing an inline search bar and selectable skill rows with rounded black checkboxes, bold skill slug, 2-line muted description, and chevron accordion; (4) 'Who gets it' scope bar with a segmented pill toggle ('This bot' / 'All bots'); (5) trust disclaimer caption and bottom action row with high-contrast black pill CTA ('Install 1 skill') and secondary outline pill ('Not now').

refs.name: pixel-plays
refs.title: Pixel Plays — 3D Pixel Games OS UI/UX
refs.tagline: Open-source 3D isometric voxel & pixel diorama games built with Claude Opus 5.5 — minimal gallery OS chrome, dithered foliage, soft directional shadows, and tactile micro-controls.
refs.stylePrompt: Design an interactive 3D isometric pixel-art diorama & mini-game OS ('Pixel Plays' style): (1) pure gallery-white full-viewport stage (#FFFFFF) that lets the isometric diorama float in negative space; (2) crisp nearest-neighbor voxel/pixel rendering with dithered grass fringes, warm timber court borders, and soft angled cast shadows; (3) ultra-minimal OS switcher pill at top-center in monospace (e.g. 'Balote ▾') with zero visual clutter; (4) responsive physics and subtle ambient particle/foliage motion.

refs.name: the-making-of-nhang
refs.title: The Making of Nhang — Illustrated Editorial UI/UX Style
refs.tagline: Warm giay-do rice-paper canvas (#F5F0E6), hand-drawn ultramarine & vermilion colored-pencil cross-hatching in plain JavaScript, bilingual notebook statechart nodes, and step-by-step playback controls.
refs.stylePrompt: Draw an interactive step-by-step illustrated diagram in plain JavaScript using 'The Making of Nhang' editorial UI/UX style: (1) warm Vietnamese giay-do rice-paper background (#F5F0E6) with subtle organic grain; (2) procedural colored-pencil & ballpoint cross-hatch illustrations in ultramarine blue (#1E3296), vermilion red (#D6382E), bamboo green (#5DBB46), and golden ochre (#E8A331) with jittered multi-pass strokes; (3) distressed typewriter slab-serif typography (Special Elite / Courier Prime) with Roman numeral chapter kicker, bold ink-bleed display title, blue italic English subtitle, and red italic Vietnamese caption; (4) lined notebook-paper statechart nodes with red margin rule, bilingual labels, wavy blue pencil bottom edge, and animated state token; (5) fixed bottom playback bar with pill buttons (restart, prev, pause, next, 3x speed) and step counter (e.g. 2/27).
